sn44.9:2.1: Compare the similar passage at [mn77:6.3](), which also introduces the six ascetic teachers.
sn44.9:5.4: The simile of the fire going out for lack of fuel is famously discussed with Vacchagotta in [mn72]().
sn44.9:6.4: This is one of several passages that acknowledge an “in-between state” after death and before rebirth. See also [sn12.11:1.3](), [sn35.87:11.8](), [sn46.3:9.5](). | In parallel phrases, _aññataraṁ_ qualifies the realm of rebirth (eg. [an6.34:1.5](): _aññataraṁ brahmalokaṁ upapanno_). This must be the meaning of the second _kāya_ here, rather than “body”. | I read _satto_ as “attached”, since one who has been freed would not be reborn.
